- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underreact to upward momentum; increase forecast slope slightly.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70.0), model often overcorrects downward; cap downward momentum at 1–2% below peak for 3–5 days.
- If official supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates upside; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast mean for 5–7 day horizon.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and supply net is negative, model flattens forecast; adjust upward by 0.3–0.8% to reflect hidden bullish bias.
- If model shows gradual upward trend but true outcome spikes sharply, model is lagging; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with 1–2% overshoot.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds 75.00, model often underestimates; add 1–3% buffer if sentiment is bullish or supply net is negative.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model overestimates; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
